name: Halvek Matcha-Tahini Coins
manufacturer: Halvek Confectionery (street brand, the Gray Zone-origin, now Tier 2-3 distributed)
description: Small pressed discs of matcha-tahini synth-candy, chalky in texture, slow-dissolving. Originally made by a single family operation in the Gray Zone's Level 4 market row, Halvek scaled up without losing the slightly rough-pressed artisan look that made them distinctive.
flavor_profile: Vegetal matcha bitterness and rich sesame paste sweetness in near-equal balance; chalky texture gives way to a smooth finish, faintly nutty and grassy simultaneously
price: Φ0.30 per coin / Φ2.50 for 10-count sleeve
slogan: Started in the Gray Zone. Stayed real.
cultural_context: Halvek coins carry genuine the Gray Zone origin credibility, which makes them aspirational to some Tier 2 consumers who want to signal authenticity. On the actual the Gray Zone, they're just candy — good, cheap, and reliable. The family that started Halvek still runs quality control from their Level 4 unit. Some the Gray Zone residents resent the brand's upward distribution as a sell-out; others are proud.
story_hooks: The Halvek family matriarch who controls the original formula has refused a buyout offer from Nalvec Consumer Goods three times — the fourth offer comes with an implicit threat.

A food journalist doing a piece on the Gray Zone-origin brands discovers the 'artisan' production story is partially fabricated at the distribution scale, but the original family is genuinely unaware of how their story is being marketed.
Someone is using Halvek coin sleeves as dead-drop containers — the sleeve dimensions fit a specific data chip exactly.
